transcript.text: A fridge that isn't getting cold can be caused by simple things like a wrong temperature setting, blocked air vents inside, or a more complex issue with the cooling system itself. To figure out which it is, I need to know: is the freezer section still cold (frozen food remains hard), and can you hear the compressor humming or the internal fan running?
freezer still freezing stuff solid. motor running a lot, maybe more than usual

Since your freezer is still freezing solid but the fridge isn't cold, and the motor is running more than usual, the cooling system itself (the compressor) is likely working fine. The problem is usually that the cold air produced in the freezer isn't reaching the fridge section. The most common reasons for this are:
1. Blocked Airflow: Cold air travels from the freezer to the fridge through vents. If these are blocked by food or tight shelving, the fridge warms up while the freezer stays cold.
2. Heat Build-up: If the condenser coils (usually at the back or bottom) are dusty or the fridge is pushed too close to a wall, it can't dissipate heat efficiently, causing the motor to run constantly and struggle to cool the fridge section. Please check if the vents inside are clear and if there is space around the appliance. Let me know what you find.
moved food away from the vents, no difference. few inches gap at the back, not dusty. no burning smell or tripping btw

Since clearing the visible vents didn't help, the issue is likely hidden. The most common cause for a warm fridge with a cold freezer (when airflow isn't blocked by food) is ice building up inside the appliance—either blocking the air channel or indicating a defrost system fault. To guide you to the right fix, I need the make and model number of your fridge-freezer. This is usually on a sticker inside the fridge compartment, often near the salad drawer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
Samsung. sticker says RB34 but the rest is rubbed off

The most likely cause now is a blocked internal air channel or drain. In frost-free Samsung fridges, defrost water drains out of the freezer into a pan at the bottom. If this drain gets blocked by food debris or ice, water can back up and freeze inside the wall, blocking the cold air vent. Please unplug the fridge for safety. Open both doors and look at the back wall inside the fridge section (usually near the bottom). Is there a small plastic drain hole or channel? If you see any standing water, ice, or frost blocking it, please clear it gently with warm water from a jug or syringe. Also, listen closely when the door is closed: do you hear a faint whirring fan running inside?
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
cant see any drain hole or standing water at the back of the fridge. no fan whirr really, just a faint scraping/ticking from the freezer sometimes

The faint scraping or ticking sound you hear is likely the evaporator fan blade hitting a block of ice hidden behind the rear panel inside the freezer. Since we can't see the drain hole, it may be blocked further down or covered in frost. 1. Unplug the appliance and remove all food (keep it cold if possible).
2. Leave both doors open for 24 hours to ensure any hidden ice behind the panels has melted.
3. Dry everything thoroughly and plug it back in. If the fridge cools down normally after this, it was a defrost issue (likely a blocked drain or failed defrost heater). If it still doesn't cool after 24 hours of defrosting, we will need to look at the fan motor.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
ok can put the food at the neighbours for a day. will do the defrost and report back

That sounds like a sensible plan. A full 24-hour defrost is the best way to clear any hidden ice blockage behind the panels that we can't see from the outside. Once you've unplugged it for the day and plugged it back in with the doors closed, please let me know if the fridge section starts cooling normally again. If it does cool down but then gets warm again after a few days, or if there is still no improvement at all, we will need to look at the defrost components (like the heater or thermostat) which would require an engineer.

You should proceed with the full defrost as planned: unplug the appliance, remove all food (keeping it cold), leave both doors open for 24 hours to let any hidden ice behind the panels melt completely, dry everything thoroughly, and then plug it back in. Once you have done this, please report back whether the fridge section starts cooling normally again.
ok will do the defrost now, back in a day or so
Please go ahead with the 24-hour defrost as planned. Once you have plugged it back in and left the doors closed for a few hours, let me know if the fridge section starts cooling normally again.
